City of Encinitas
Regular City Council Meeting - 6:00 p.m.
AGENDA
WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 13, 2019 -
06:00 PM
p.m.
City of Encinitas - City Council Chambers
505 S. Vulcan Avenue
Encinitas, California 92024
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council.
1.
CALL TO ORDER
2.
ROLL CALL
3.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
4.
SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS AND PROCLAMATIONS
4A.
Presentation by the Public Works Department regarding the Sanitary Sewer Management Plan.
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a “WHITE” speaker slip to the City Clerk. If needed, Oral Communication items will be referred to the City Manager either for resolution by administrative action or placement on a future agenda.
6.
REPORT FROM CLOSED SESSION (IF HELD)
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a “WHITE” speaker slip to the City Clerk. If needed, Oral Communication items will be referred to the City Manager either for resolution by administrative action or placement on a future agenda.
7.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act.
The title of ordinances listed on this agenda are deemed to have been read and further reading waived.
8.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a “PINK” speaker slip to the City Clerk. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
8A.
Approval of the Minutes of the October 23, 2019 Regular Meeting, and the October 30, 2019 Special-Closed Session Meeting. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
Approve the Minutes.
2019-11-13 Item 08A Minutes
8B.
Approval of the Warrants List. Contact Person: Finance Manager Lundgren
Approve the Warrants.
2019-11-13 Item 08B Warrants
8C.
Youth Commission Work Plan Outcomes for Fiscal Year 2018-19 and Proposed Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2019-20. Contact Person: Recreation Supervisor Hernandez
1) Receive final report outcomes for Fiscal Year 2018-19 Youth Commission Work Plan; and 2) Approve the proposed Fiscal Year 2019-20 Youth Commission Work Plan.
2019-11-13 Item 08C Youth Commission Work Plan Outcomes for Fiscal Year 2018-19 and Proposed Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2019-20
8D.
Reclassifying one (1) Senior Engineer position to a City Traffic Engineer classification. Contact Person: Human Resources Analyst Chase
Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution 2019-92 approving the reclassification of one (1) Senior Engineer position to a City Traffic Engineer Position.
2019-11-13 Item 08D Reclassifying One Senior Engineer position to a City Traffic Engineer Classification
8E.
Amendment to As-Needed Information Technology (IT) Security and Disaster Recovery (DR) Contract. Contact Person: IT Operations Supervisor Contreras
1) Authorize the City Manager, in coordination with the City Attorney, to amend a Professional Services Contract, in substantial form with Nth Generation for a term of one-year with option to extend one additional one-year period, for a total not-to-exceed amount of $150,000 for as-needed IT services; and 2) Authorize the IT Manager to execute any necessary task orders associated with the fully executed As-Needed IT Security and Disaster Recovery contracts with Nth Generation within the granted authority.
2019-11-13 Item 08E Amendment to As Needed IT Security and Disaster Recovery Contract
8F.
Agreement for Managed Information Technology Services by and between the City of Encinitas and the San Elijo Powers Authority effective January 3, 2020. Contact Person: IT Operations Supervisor Contreras
1) Approve the Agreement for Information Technology (IT) Managed Services by and between the City of Encinitas and the San Elijo Joint Powers Authority (SEJPA) in substantial form in consultation with the City Attorney; 2) Authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement on behalf of the City of Encinitas; 3) Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2019-89 amending the FY 2019-20 budget to appropriate $37,796 to the Information Technology Operating Budget and $46,350 to the Revenue Budget; and 4) Authorize the City Manager to execute any necessary change order amendments associated with the fully executed contract within the granted authority.
2019-11-13 Item 08F Agreement with SEJPA for Managed Information Technology Services
8G.
Additional funding for the El Camino Real Mobility and Striping Improvements (CS20B) Project. Contact Person: Principal Engineer Bankston
Adopt Resolution No. 2019-97, entitled “A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas Amending the Fiscal Year 2019-20 Budget,” to allocate $76,722 to the El Camino Real Mobility and Striping Improvements (CS20B) project.
2019-11-13 Item 08G Additional Funding for the El Camino Real Mobility and Striping Improvments (CS20B) Project
8H.
Letter of support for a San Diego County Botanic Garden grant funding opportunity. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Ratify the attached Letter of support for a San Diego County Botanic Garden grant funding opportunity.
2019-11-13 Item 08H Botanic Gardens Letter of Support
8I.
Contract Amendments for Leucadia Streetscape Project (CS04D) contract with MW Peltz & Associates for landscape and irrigation services. Contact Person: Principal Engineer Bankston
1) Ratify Amendment #3 of the Leucadia Streetscape Project (CS04D) contract with MW Peltz & Associates executed on March 30, 2010 for $47,300 for preparation of Phase 1 options; 2) Ratify Amendment #5 of the Leucadia Streetscape Project (CS04D) contract with MW Peltz & Associates executed on February 8, 2010 for $21,400 for preparation of tree planting plans; 3) Ratify Amendment #7 of the Leucadia Streetscape Project (CS04D) contract with MW Peltz & Associates executed on May 5, 2014 for $16,170 for updating the traffic analysis of Alternative 5; and 4) Authorize the City Manager, or designee, in coordination with the City Attorney, to execute a contract amendment and extensions, with MW Peltz & Associates in the amount of $161,445 plus 15 percent contingency for a total contract amendment amount not to exceed $185,662 and a total contract cost not to exceed $1,032,962 to update landscaping and irrigation plans to reflect the temporary east side option and to accommodate the current civil design.
2019-11-13 Item 08I Contract Amendments for Leucadia Streetscape Project (CS04D) with MW Peltz & Associates
9.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR Staff reports will be given only if requested by the person who pulled the item.
10.
ACTION ITEMS
10A.
Adoption of City Council Ordinance No. 2019-23 to adopt the Modification suggested by the California Coastal Commission to City Council Ordinance No. 2019-01, which amended the Zoning Code and Local Coastal Program to allow Emergency Shelters as a Permitted Use in the Business Park and Light Industrial Zones. Contact Person: Principal Planner Gates
Adopt City Council Ordinance No. 2019-23 titled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, Adopting the Modification Suggested by the California Coastal Commission to City Council Ordinance No. 2019-01, Amending Section 30.36.020(B) of Chapter 30.36 Emergency Shelters.”
2019-11-13 Item 10A Emergency Shelter CCC Modification
10B.
Adoption of City Council Ordinance No. 2019-21 and Ordinance No. 2019-22. Ordinance No. 2019-21 adopts the 2019 California Building Standards Code, as required by law, which will take effect January 1, 2020. Ordinance No. 2019-22 proposed Municipal Code amendments to implement the Encinitas Climate Action Plan’s strategy related to electric vehicle charging. CASE NOS: PLCY-003360-2019 and APLAN-0000-15-2018 ZA; LOCATION: Citywide. Contact Person: Principal Planner Smith
1) Adopt City Council Ordinance No. 2019-21, titled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California adopting Amendments to Chapter 23.12 (Uniform Codes for Construction) of Title 23 (Building and Construction) of the Encinitas Municipal Code to adopt the 2019 California Building Standards Code with certain amendments, additions, and deletions;” and 2) Adopt City Council Ordinance No. 2019-22, titled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, adopting Amendments to Chapter 23.12 (Uniform Codes for Construction) of Title 23 (Building and Construction) of the Encinitas Municipal Code to implement the City of Encinitas Climate Action Plan’s Strategy related to electric vehicle charging.”
2019-11-13 Item 10B Second Reading Building Code & EV Charging Amendments
10C.
Adoption of Ordinance 2019-27, which adopts the 2018 International Fire Code and the 2019 California Fire Code with certain amendments, additions, and deletions. Contact Person: Senior Deputy Fire Marshal Berberet
Adopt City Council Ordinance No. 2019-27, titled “An Ordinance of the City of Encinitas which repeals Chapter 10.04 of the City of Encinitas Municipal Code and adopts a new Chapter 10.04 adopting the 2018 International Fire Code and 2019 California Fire Code with certain amendments, additions, and deletions.”
2019-11-13 Item 10C Ordinance 2019-27 Adoption of Fire Code
10D.
Introduction of Ordinances No. 2019-24, No. 2019-25, and No. 2019-26 for amendments to Title 4, 14, 24, and 30 of the Encinitas Municipal Code and the Local Coastal Plan to modify design requirements and development standards for Pedestrian and Bicycle Connectivity (Ordinance No. 2019-24), to limit the number of dogs allowed in residential districts or in conjunction with any residential use in any other district (Ordinance No. 2019-25), and to modify existing traffic code regulations (Ordinance 2019-26). Contact Person: Associate Planner Zornes
1) Introduce City Council Ordinance No. 2019-24 titled “An Ordinance of the City of Encinitas Adopting Amendments to Title 24 (Subdivisions), Title 30 (Zoning) of the Encinitas Municipal Code, and Local Coastal Plan, to Modify Design Requirements and Development Standards for Pedestrian and Bicycle Connectivity;” 2) Introduce City Council Ordinance No. 2019-25 titled “An Ordinance of the City of Encinitas Adopting Amendments to Title 4 (Animal Regulations) of the Encinitas Municipal Code, to Limit the Number of Dogs Allowed in all Residential Districts or in Conjunction with any Residential Uses in any other district;” and 3) Introduce City Council Ordinance No. 2019-26 titled “An Ordinance of the City of Encinitas Adopting Amendments to Title 14 (Traffic Code) of the Encinitas Municipal Code, to Modify Existing Traffic Code Regulations.”
2019-11-13 Item 10D Priority Code Amendments
2019-11-13 Item 10D Priority Code Amendments - Minor Modifications
10E.
2019 Legislative Review and Update to Legislative Priorities. Contact Person: Mayor/Legislative Liaison Blakespear and Senior Management Analyst Piatt
1) Receive the 2019 Legislative Session Report; and 2) Approve the update to the Council's Legislative Priorities.
2019-11-13 Item 10E 2019 Legislative Review and Update to Legislative Priorities
2019-11-13 Item 10E Legislative Review and Update to Legislative Priorities - Minor Modifications

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
